Gustave Flaubert, Salammbô, translated by J. S. Chartres.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/gustave-flaubert/salammbo/j-s-chartres

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Gustave Flaubert, the author, died 1880 (Wikidata Q43444, P570 1880-05-08).
- J. S. Chartres, the translator, died 1927 (Wikidata Q24196976, P570 1927-05-14).

First publication of the text used: 1886, the English translation by J. S. Chartres. The French original was published in 1862. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'Salammbô was published in 1862 by Gustave Flaubert. It was translated from French in 1886 by J. S. Chartres.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1886 and the original in 1862, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: French work by Gustave Flaubert (died 1880), first published 1862. The author died before 1926, so the original is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator J. S. Chartres (died 1927) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 1998, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/gustave-flaubert/salammbo/j-s-chartres): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q43444 (Gustave Flaubert), P570 1880-05-08.
